guide.shared_stock_exchange.page.1.title: What this is
guide.shared_stock_exchange.page.1.body:
Shared Stock Exchange lets everyone on the server trade the same prices.
Cash is EMC from ProjectE: buying takes EMC, selling pays EMC back.
Without ProjectE the mod uses a built-in test wallet; install it and your EMC is used automatically.
Prices live in the server save, so every player sees identical quotes.
guide.shared_stock_exchange.page.2.title: Getting the terminal
guide.shared_stock_exchange.page.2.body:
Stock Trading Terminal recipe: 4 iron ingots, 4 redstone, 1 glass pane (iron-redstone-iron / redstone-glass-redstone / iron-redstone-iron).
Right click to open the exchange, sneak + right click to read this handbook.
It is also in the creative tab.
The handbook itself is crafted from 1 book and 1 redstone (shapeless).
guide.shared_stock_exchange.page.3.title: Reading the screen
guide.shared_stock_exchange.page.3.body:
Each row is one stock: name, price, change, market cap, holdings, profit and the recent trend.
Green means up and red means down; the small bar at the start of each row means the same.
The Qty box at the top decides how many shares; type a number or use 1 / 10 / 100 / 1000.
Hover a row to see the largest holder, the dividend pool, both switches, and the EMC left after this trade.
Click the theme chip at the top to switch colours; click a row to open the chart page.
guide.shared_stock_exchange.page.4.title: Trading rules
guide.shared_stock_exchange.page.4.body:
Buys fill at market price; the more you buy the higher the average price, and heavy selling pushes the price down.
Asking for more shares than the market can sell fills for everything that is available instead of failing.
Asking to sell more shares than you own sells all of them, so you never have to count your shares first.
A tenth of every stock is never sold, so the price cannot be pushed to the sky.
Every trade takes a 1% fee that goes into that stock's dividend pool.
All trades settle on the server; the client only sends requests.
guide.shared_stock_exchange.page.5.title: Reading the chart
guide.shared_stock_exchange.page.5.body:
Click any row to open that stock's price chart.
The line shows the last 120 prices and every segment has its own color: green when that step went up, red when it went down.
The area color, the border and the badge in the top right still show the trend of the whole window.
High (light green), low (light red), the white dashed start price and the gold average cost line are marked.
Move the mouse to the left or right edge of the chart and arrows appear; click to switch stock. Arrow keys work too.
guide.shared_stock_exchange.page.6.title: Debt and forced liquidation
guide.shared_stock_exchange.page.6.body:
Buying with short cash is allowed: ProjectE's EMC is simply charged below zero, and the exchange panel, the ProjectE panel and the transmutation table all show that same minus sign (/stock debt off disables it).
While it is negative, selling items in the transmutation table refills it towards zero: you must sell the equivalent value before it reaches 0 - that is the punishment for a bad trade.
You still need some cushion: an order that would drop you below the margin line right away is refused (unless forced liquidation is off).
When you owe money and equity falls below the margin line, forced liquidation sells every share to repay it.
Forced liquidation has its own switch (/stock liquidation off); with it off the debt just sits there.
Only online players are settled: prices keep moving while you are offline.
guide.shared_stock_exchange.page.7.title: Dividends
guide.shared_stock_exchange.page.7.body:
The dividend pool is funded by the 1% fee on every trade.
Every 10 minutes the server splits the pool by holdings: online players are paid at once, offline players get it when they log in.
You can also click Collect or run /stock claim.
guide.shared_stock_exchange.page.8.title: Liquidation and pace
guide.shared_stock_exchange.page.8.body:
Sell all on the market screen sells everything; Clear on a detail page sells one stock.
Commands: /stock clear for all, /stock clear <stock> for one.
Prices move every 30 s by default; admins can set 5-3600 s with /stock interval 60. In singleplayer you can change it yourself.
guide.shared_stock_exchange.page.9.title: Multiplayer and commands
guide.shared_stock_exchange.page.9.body:
Everyone shares one order book: your big buy pushes the price up, someone's sell pushes it down.
/stock list shows prices, /stock mine your holdings, /stock top the richest players (cash + holdings).
/stock chart <stock> draws the trend in chat; /stock buy <stock> <shares> and /stock sell <stock> <shares> trade without opening the UI.
/stock refund resets a debt; /stock debt on|off toggles the debt system; /stock liquidation on|off toggles forced liquidation.
/stock status shows the ProjectE self-check plus both switches, your equity, debt and margin line.

command.shared_stock_exchange.status_mar: Equity %1$s   Debt %2$s   Margin line %3$s (below it you get liquidated)
guide.shared_stock_exchange.page.10.body:
"Test wallet" at the top: ProjectE is not installed, so the built-in wallet is used.
"ProjectE not connected": it is installed but did not answer; run /stock status for the self-check.
Negative EMC: that is your debt, and ProjectE's own panel and transmutation table show the same negative number. Sell items in the table or sell shares to fill it back; /stock refund resets you (holdings are wiped too).
Do not want more debt? /stock debt off. Do not want automatic selling? /stock liquidation off.
"Would trip the margin line": the order is too big and would be liquidated at once, so it is refused.
"Cannot afford": the debt system is off and your cash is short. "Interface did not answer": nothing was traded.
The test wallet was cleared: use /stock wallet 1000000 in a singleplayer world to restart.

guide.shared_stock_exchange.page.11.body:
With the debt system on (default) you can keep buying with short cash, and ProjectE's EMC itself goes negative - the exchange panel, the ProjectE panel and the transmutation table all show that minus sign, there is no separate ledger.
While it is negative, selling items in the transmutation table adds EMC towards 0: owing 500 means you must sell 500 worth before it reaches zero.
The catch is the margin line: an order that would trip it right away is refused, so an account already in the red with no shares cannot buy until it sells its way back.
Debt does not vanish by itself: selling shares and collecting dividends fill the negative balance first, and EMC earned in the transmutation table does too.
With /stock debt off you can only spend cash and existing negative EMC is cleared automatically.
The trade preview tells you in advance: green means you stay debt free, orange means the trade leaves you in debt.
guide.shared_stock_exchange.page.12.body:
/stock refund: while the EMC is negative, one use wipes your holdings and the negative balance and resets EMC to 1000.
Why holdings go too: otherwise you could buy shares on credit, refund to 1000 and keep the shares - free money.
/stock debt on|off: the debt system switch - can you keep buying with short cash and drive EMC negative? On by default.
/stock liquidation on|off: the forced liquidation switch - sell shares automatically below the margin line? On by default.
They are independent and saved with the world; only ops or the singleplayer host can change them. Bare /stock debt shows the state.
guide.shared_stock_exchange.page.13.body:
Equity = EMC + what all your shares would fetch if sold now (never price x shares, which overstates it).
While you owe money and equity falls below 10% of that liquidation value (the margin line), the server checks every second and sells everything to repay the debt.
To avoid instant liquidations, orders that would drop you below the line are refused up front while both switches are on.
With forced liquidation off nothing is sold automatically - but the negative EMC stays and blocks new buys.
To start over completely: /stock refund, or /stock wallet 1000000 in singleplayer.
guide.shared_stock_exchange.page.14.body:
The "Settings" chip next to the title opens the settings screen: theme, debt system, forced liquidation, update interval, test wallet, minor refund and the up/down chart colours all live there.
Toggles apply server-wide at once and are saved; the interval and test wallet need an admin or the singleplayer host.
The minor refund asks twice: it clears holdings and the negative EMC and resets EMC to 1000.
Chart colours default to green up / red down; pick a swatch or type #RRGGBB and press Apply.
Each list row has a colour bar on the left: green up, red down; the bottom line previews the EMC left after this trade.
Selling more than you own sells everything, just like buying more than the market has buys everything.
message.shared_stock_exchange.no_shares: You do not hold this stock yet; buy some first
gui.shared_stock_exchange.theme_tip: Light / dark theme and chart colours live there too
guide.shared_stock_exchange.page.15.body:
The settings screen (the "Settings" chip next to the title) carries every /stock setting over to the GUI.
Theme: light / dark, switchable at any time, saved under config/.
Debt system: whether EMC can go negative (written straight into ProjectE, so the transmutation table shows it too), on by default.
Forced liquidation: whether stocks are auto-sold when equity breaks the maintenance line, on by default.
Update interval: how often prices move, 5-3600 seconds like the command.
Test wallet: only visible without ProjectE, a way to start over in singleplayer.
Minor refund: in debt, confirm twice; clears holdings and the negative EMC, EMC back to 1000.
Chart colours: default green up / red down; pick a swatch or type #RRGGBB.
It changes the colour role, not a texture: sparkline, big chart, numbers and the row bars all follow it, and anything new that uses the up/down role follows automatically.
Colours and theme are stored in small files under config/; delete them to return to defaults.
Tooltip text can only use the 16 built-in chat colours, so it picks the closest one to your custom colour.
guide.shared_stock_exchange.page.16.titl: The Stocks app on your phone
guide.shared_stock_exchange.page.16.body:
With MCphone (the 1.20.1 Forge build) installed, a Stocks app shows up on the phone home screen.
It opens a live price list: one row per stock, the side bar and the change colour follow the price; tap a row for the chart, your holdings and your profit or loss.
Pick an amount at the bottom (1 / 10 / 100 / all, or nudge it with - and +) and press Buy or Sell to trade at the market price.
The phone and the trading terminal share the same prices and the same EMC, so there is never a second price.
The phone's Library app also lists this Shared Stock Exchange Guide, so the tutorial travels with you.
Without MCphone nothing changes: the terminal, commands and screens behave exactly as before.
Both the list and the detail page have a "Big" button in the top-right corner that switches to the full trading screen. The full screen has a "Phone" button at the bottom to go back. Switch freely in either direction.
